title: Taiwan to impose strict controls on AI chip exports to China
source_used: Taiwan News (relaying a Bloomberg interview, CNA and Reuters)
key_facts: Taiwan Economics Minister Kung Ming-hsin said Taiwan plans to add advanced semiconductors and AI servers to its export control list, bringing its rules closer to US restrictions.
Unauthorised shipments of restricted equipment could then bring criminal charges under the Foreign Trade Act.
The changes are part of commitments under the Taiwan-US Agreement on Reciprocal Trade.
Kung said some controls would follow US rules but did not say when the new measures take effect.
CNA reported that current rules require permits for sensitive technologies, but advanced AI chips and servers are not specifically covered, so some unauthorised shipments are hard to prosecute.
In August, prosecutors indicted nine people over an alleged scheme to export AI servers to China: 130 servers, 74 allegedly sent through other countries with false documents.
Those charges were breach of trust and document forgery rather than export offences.
Reuters reported that a contractor linked to Super Micro Computer pleaded guilty in a US case over diverting Nvidia-powered AI servers to China.
quote_evidence: Taiwan plans to tighten controls on advanced AI chips and servers exported to China, bringing its rules closer to US restrictions, Economics Minister Kung Ming-hsin (龔明鑫) said.
Unauthorized shipments of restricted equipment could then lead to criminal charges under the Foreign Trade Act, the minister said.
He said some export controls would follow US rules but did not say when the new measures would take effect.
why_it_matters_hint: Taiwan's existing rules do not clearly cover AI chips and servers, so smuggling cases have been hard to prosecute.
notes: Bloomberg original (bloomberg.com, 16 Oct 2026) is paywalled; read Taiwan News, which relays it. Taiwan News calls it 'a Monday interview'; Bloomberg's story is dated Friday 16 Oct 2026 05:49 GMT, so the day of the interview is unclear. Pool headline said 'strict controls'; the facts are a plan with no start date.
